verdict_basis: No Definition-of-Done item is unmet outright, and two are partial. Scenario A has been reproduced by an operator other than its author, which was the last thing no amount of code could supply. What remains is documentation a stranger can follow without deviation, and a Scenario B run.

items.requirement: README states the evidence-driven reproduction mission and the difference from Microsoft Learn
items.evidence: README.md opens by distinguishing this guide from Microsoft Learn and links the evidence model.

items.requirement: Repository-wide KEEP / REWRITE / MOVE / DELETE / ARCHIVE audit completed
items.evidence: 19 paths decided in docs/reference/golden-repository-audit.json: 16 KEEP, 3 ARCHIVE, 0 DELETE. The single REWRITE was resolved during the epic and became KEEP.

items.requirement: AGENTS.md rewritten around agent judgment; machine-enforceable rules moved to validators/CI where possible
items.evidence: AGENTS.md is organised around this repository's mission across eight sections, opening on Mission and reaching the evidence rules by line 35, down from 1275 lines to 1070 with the series contract moved to docs/meta/series-contract.md rather than deleted. The documented-but-unenforced rules are now enforced: the frontmatter scope rule, the deployment-method sub-template, and the Golden suites all run in a pull-request-scoped job. Auditing the remaining prose found three checks that disagreed with the policy they implemented rather than documentation debt, and the quality gate now passes across all 234 files with --all wired into CI so it stays there.

items.requirement: Common Evidence / Assertion / Hypothesis representations exist
items.evidence: Five schemas under schemas/golden/ cover evidence, assertion, manifest, result and reproduction. evidence.schema.json declares the identity and capture time of raw observations, which is what lets the evaluator reject evidence from another run.

items.requirement: Execution status separated from hypothesis status
items.evidence: EXECUTION_STATUS and HYPOTHESIS_STATUS are separate frozen vocabularies in scripts/golden/evaluate_run.py. A run that did not execute cannot report a hypothesis verdict.

items.requirement: Raw evidence separated from generated verdict; run identity exists
items.evidence: The result contract carries run identity and the evaluator derives the verdict from assertion outcomes rather than accepting an asserted one.
captured_at, evaluated_at and document_updated_at are distinct fields. This is the ACA defect where re-evaluation time was stamped into a field named for capture.

items.requirement: Negative tests: missing, empty, malformed, contradictory, wrong-run, recovery-missing, comparison-semantics mismatch
items.evidence: tests/golden/test_negative_evidence.py covers missing, empty, malformed, contradictory, wrong-run, recovery-missing and comparison-semantics cases across 24 tests. The wrong-run case compares evidence identity against the manifest run_id and was confirmed to fail when the identity check is removed.

items.requirement: Golden scenarios A (deterministic), B (comparative), C (configuration/state) completed
items.evidence: Two of three scenarios have been executed against a live subscription. Scenario A's run 20260927T104304Z evaluates to SUPPORTED under the Golden model. Scenario C's run 20260927T114621Z evaluates to INCONCLUSIVE: five assertions held and two could not be observed, so the model declined a verdict rather than supplying one. All three manifests are satisfiable and every collector is held by a suite proving its evidence can refuse the hypothesis.
items.gap: Scenario B has not been executed; nothing yet persists its per-phase probe records or probes the destination's own health. Scenario C's run could not observe slot stickiness because the destination worker still predated the swap, and nothing queries deployment error rows. Both gaps are recorded against the runs rather than implied.

items.requirement: Independent reproduction completed for at least one scenario
items.evidence: An independent operator reproduced Scenario A. Given only the published documentation and the target commit, without the authoring session's reasoning or root-cause analysis, it deployed fresh infrastructure and obtained SUPPORTED, matching run 20260927T104304Z without being told the expected answer. Its replay run is 20260927T223558Z-e391956951c1 and it confirmed its own cleanup. check_reproduction reports reproduction_result REPRODUCED.
items.gap: documentation_result is FAILED, so the gate does not pass. The reproducer recorded five deviations: the lab guide and the evidence model state contradictory exit-code meanings, cleanup.sh is absent from the published runbook, the model describes a run directory of manifest.json and evidence.json while this scenario writes run.json and phase directories, run.py --help omits positional arguments, and the runbook interleaves historical observed values with current procedure. The hypothesis reproduced; the documentation did not.

items.requirement: Cleanup procedure exists and is verified
items.evidence: cleanup.sh was executed against the live deployment. It refused to run without an explicit target, exiting 2, then deleted the resource group; az group exists reported false 90 seconds later. Deleting the group rather than enumerating resources is what keeps the procedure complete as the template changes.

docs/reference/golden-evidence-model.md states the historical evidence policy: how long a capture stays authoritative, what re-verification requires, and that a capture predating the contract it is cited under is trusted-historical rather than primary. Both Golden scenarios classify their retained captures accordingly.

items.requirement: Legacy labs classified Golden / migration-needed / archive-candidate
items.evidence: All 12 labs classified in labs/golden-classification.json: 2 golden, 9 migration-needed, 1 archive-candidate. Coverage is asserted in both directions so neither an unclassified lab nor an orphan entry passes.

items.requirement: README validation/maturity wording matches actual evidence
items.evidence: Lab-validated became Evidence-retained, the legend names both missing conditions, and the lab count was corrected from 10 to 12. The guard fails once a reproduction or completed run exists, forcing the claim to be re-decided rather than staying forbidden after it becomes true.

items.requirement: Existing documentation quality gates do not regress
items.evidence: 12 required checks pass on PR 186 and one is skipped, including Build Documentation, which runs mkdocs build --strict and confirms the nav entries this branch adds. PII reports 0 blocking, repetition 0 errors across 233 files, and frontmatter validation exits 0.

blocking_for_v1: Item 10: the hypothesis reproduced independently but the documentation did not; five deviations are recorded.
Item 9: Scenario B has not completed a live run.
notes: Item 10 needs a person other than the operator who produced the runs; no amount of further code satisfies it. Item 9 needs Scenario B instrumented to persist per-phase probe records and probe the destination's own health, after which it can run. Scenario C's run left two observations absent and returned INCONCLUSIVE, which is the model working rather than failing.

findings_accepted: evaluate_run.py keyed assertion outcomes by caller-supplied id, so a duplicate id dropped a CONTRADICTED outcome and reported SUPPORTED. Reproduced, fixed, pinned.
check_reproduction.py treated equal NOT_TESTED statuses as REPRODUCED, so two runs that never happened reproduced each other. Reproduced, fixed, pinned.
No workflow ran tests/golden, so 134 tests protected nothing in CI.
validate_frontmatter.py was wired into a job gated on push to main, so it never ran on a pull request.
Items 4 and 8 overstated: no Evidence schema exists and no wrong-run test exists.
Item 15 said all 13 checks pass; 12 pass and one is skipped.
verdict_basis said four partial items while the counts said three.
Mutation verification is asserted in prose with no retained artifact.

Auditing the quality gate's 29 standing errors found three checks disagreeing with the policy they implemented: the deployment sub-template had no carve-out, the CLI explanation-table rule was applied to yaml fences though AGENTS.md scopes it to bash, and playbook sections were matched exactly though AGENTS.md permits a trailing qualifier. 29 errors to 0, each fix mutation-verified.

Building a contract-to-collector alignment check found that no Golden manifest in the repository is satisfiable: all three declare fields no collector emits, and two disclosed nothing while the third understated the gap as one missing field when all five were missing. Scenario A additionally carries two parallel contract systems, so its real Azure run satisfied run.py's contract rather than its Golden manifest.

Scenario A's Golden manifest is now satisfiable and satisfied: a collector bridges the runner's contract to it, and the real Azure run evaluates to SUPPORTED under the Golden model rather than only under run.py's own criteria.

All three contracts are now collectable, closing the finding that none was satisfiable. The check that found it was itself corrected twice: it associated collectors by filename convention and missed one, and it inferred whether a scenario had run from a manifest template that always ships NOT_RUN. Both now rest on declared facts, a LAB constant and an executed_runs list, rather than inference.

Executing Scenario C found two defects in its own collector that only a real run could surface. It read stickiness from a slot still serving the pre-swap worker, and it compared rollback snapshots whole, so a restart timestamp that must change made every rollback look like a mismatch. Both produced a confident CONTRADICTED that the evidence did not support; corrected, the same run is INCONCLUSIVE.

Splitting the trust field into retention_status and capture_provenance closed the two-vocabulary finding; a classification had been holding values from both axes in one field. A second Scenario C run aimed at the remaining observations failed to close them and instead exposed two more places where absence was being read as refutation: a restart boundary set at the swap's return rather than its start, and an unreachable slot compared as though it held a configuration.

Independent reproduction was obtained. A separate agent, given only published docs and the commit, reproduced Scenario A's SUPPORTED verdict against fresh infrastructure. It also demonstrated the value of separating the two axes: the hypothesis reproduced while the documentation failed, five concrete defects being the reason.
findings_disputed: The reproduction gate was called vacuously satisfiable on a fabricated record. The specific invocation shown passed a dict where check() takes a path, and the cited output keys do not exist. The underlying NOT_TESTED equality defect was real and is fixed.

The tail-section rule was reported as violated by docs/reference/validation-status.md. validate_doc_quality.py:286 exempts that file explicitly as a generated dashboard, matching this repository's stated policy for generated output, and the validator already runs ungated on pull requests. Acting on the finding would have broken correct behaviour to satisfy it.

A separate tail-section validator was implied to be missing. validate_doc_quality.py has checked tail order and ordering since before this branch; building another would have duplicated an existing gate rather than closing a gap.
